_meta.description: Tactical 24h schedule the Phase-2 office simulation reads each simulated work day. agent-runner.js's runWorkDayCycle() iterates `blocks` in order within a single invocation (no per-block cron yet — see 'cron_status'). Each block represents a point in the simulated day where a specific activity fires, so the day's ~50-case CRM pool, meetings, AI-experience reports, and spare time are spread out instead of all happening at once.
_meta.cron_status: LIVE (re-enabled 2026-07-18 for the Q&A engine's first activation, after the 2026-07-08 pause). OFFICE HOURS since 2026-08-06: wrangler.toml carries TWO Cloudflare Cron Triggers ('*/30 5-14 * * *' and '0 15 * * *') = every 30 min from 05:00 to 15:00 UTC = 08:00-18:00 IDT inclusive, 21 ticks/day. The second expression exists solely to catch the 18:00 boundary tick without also firing at 18:30, which a single '*/30 5-15' would. This REPLACES the 2026-07-18 window ('*/30 0-13,23 * * *' = 02:00-16:30 Israel, 30 ticks/day), which was set to the owner's own activity window rather than to office hours; all case_batch blocks that sat before 08:00 were retimed into the window in the same change — see _office_hours_retime_2026_08_06 below. Each tick, agent-runner.js's scheduled() converts event.scheduledTime to Israel local time (israelTimeParts()) and calls runScheduledBlock(env, time, dayOfWeek), which is a no-op unless a block below has that exact `time` for that day-of-week (note: the 02:00-Israel blocks therefore fire at 23:00 UTC the PREVIOUS calendar day — israelTimeParts() handles the day-of-week rollover). Day-in-progress state lives in SIM_KV under 'daily-cycle-state' between blocks. Per-block errors (e.g. Gemini 429) are logged to `reports` (logScheduledError) and do not abort the day.

week_mapping.description: dayOfWeek = ((current_day - 1) % 7) + 1, as already computed by runWorkDayCycle(). This schedule maps it to an Israeli Sun-Thu work week per the Launch Decisions ('work days Sunday-Thursday'), with Friday as a short summary day and Saturday off.
week_mapping.6: Friday (short day — weekly summary meeting, reduced case load)
week_mapping.7: Saturday (off for the office simulation — no case batches, no meetings, no routine Q&A Gemini/Claude calls. NOT a zero-API-calls day since the Guides feature added a weekly verification pass here — see saturday_schedule.blocks / guides_program.)

_meta.case_volume_design_note: SUPERSEDED 2026-07-18 (Q&A-engine rebuild) — volume is no longer a fixed per-agent quota at all. Once per day, at cycle start, agent-runner.js's computeDailyQuestionVolume() checks the remaining shared Claude budget for the month (config/token-economy.json shared_claude_budget) and picks a conservative day total from it (0 if exhausted) — never a fixed number decided in advance. That total is then SPREAD across the day exactly as before, via the existing case_batch case_share proportions below (6 case_batch blocks, 08:00-15:00 Israel since the 2026-08-06 office-hours retime — was 02:00-15:00 — roughly 90 minutes apart; full_day_schedule has 11 blocks total — the 6 case batches plus tool_task_window, chore_rotation, report, standup meeting, and spare_time). Non-burstiness for Notebook-X specifically doesn't come from this per-day total at all — it comes from workers/gemini-pacer.js's per-call pacing check at ask time (agent-base.js askAssignedProject()), which is what actually rate-limits Gemini calls regardless of how many questions a block was handed.

_office_hours_retime_2026_08_06.what: All case_batch blocks that sat before 08:00 Israel were moved into the 08:00-18:00 office-hours window, in the same change that narrowed the Cloudflare cron to that window (wrangler.toml: '*/30 5-14 * * *' + '0 15 * * *' = 08:00-18:00 IDT).
_office_hours_retime_2026_08_06.why: This file already declared work_hours.start = 08:00 while scheduling case batches at 02:00, 04:30 and 07:00 — hours before its own stated start. The blocks never matched the declaration. Narrowing the cron did not break the schedule's intent; it exposed a contradiction the file had been carrying. Owner decision 2026-08-06: retime the blocks to agree with the declaration rather than widen the cron back out.
_office_hours_retime_2026_08_06.volume_is_UNCHANGED_and_that_is_the_poin: NO case_share VALUE WAS EDITED. The block COUNT per schedule is unchanged (6 Sun-Thu, 3 Friday) and each block kept its original share, in its original order — only `time` moved. Sun-Thu still sums to 1.00 (0.20/0.15/0.15/0.15/0.15/0.20) and Friday still sums to 1.00 (0.40/0.30/0.30). This matters because partitionCasesByShare() (workers/agent-runner.js L1203) allocates each batch its slice of the day total UP FRONT and does not redistribute a slice whose block never fires: had the pre-dawn blocks simply been left outside the new cron window, 50% of a Sun-Thu day's questions and 70% of a Friday's would have been silently DROPPED, not deferred. Retiming preserves the day's volume exactly; leaving them would have cut it in half.
_office_hours_retime_2026_08_06.spread_not_bunched: The batches were re-spread across the window rather than packed into the earliest free slots (owner constraint). Sun-Thu batches now run 08:00, 09:30, 11:00, 12:00, 13:30, 15:00 — roughly 90-minute spacing, interleaved with the 11:30 tool-task window and 12:30 chore rotation, which did not move because both were already inside the window. Friday's three run 08:00, 09:00, 10:00, finishing 30 minutes before its 10:30 report block.
_office_hours_retime_2026_08_06.block_order_is_load_bearing: runScheduledBlock() derives isFirstBlock from blocks[0].time and isLastBlock from blocks[last].time (agent-runner.js L1839-1840) — the first entry OPENS the day cycle and the last entry FINALIZES it. Each `blocks` array below is therefore kept sorted by time. A future edit that appends a block out of order, or that moves the earliest/latest time without reordering the array, will break day open/close rather than just misplace a block.
_office_hours_retime_2026_08_06.saturday_unchanged: Saturday's two blocks were already at 08:00 — the new window's first tick — so they did not move and Saturday remains a zero-simulation-activity day.
_office_hours_retime_2026_08_06.every_block_time_must_land_on_a_cron_tic: Ticks fire at :00 and :30 only, from 08:00 to 18:00 Israel inclusive. A block at any other minute, or outside that range, is simply never reached — runScheduledBlock() matches on an exact time string.

work_hours._corrected_2026_08_06: Was 08:00-16:00. Widened to match the office-hours cron window (08:00-18:00 Israel) so this file stops disagreeing with itself — owner decision 2026-08-06. NOTE: neither this field nor overtime_window below is read by any code; both are documentation. Behaviour comes from the cron window plus the `blocks` times, which is exactly why the two were able to drift apart unnoticed in the first place.

overtime_window.note: Per-agent overtime eligibility comes from agents-config.json work_routine.overtime (e.g. agent_2 '30%_of_days', agent_5 'regular', agent_10 'daily'). Overtime cases are drawn from the same daily pool via extendSession(), not a separate pool.
overtime_window._relationship_to_work_hours_2026_08_06: This window now sits INSIDE work_hours rather than after it, and that is deliberate, not a leftover. Read it as: the office is OPEN 08:00-18:00, and 16:00-18:00 is the portion of that only overtime-eligible agents work. Before 2026-08-06 work_hours ended at 16:00 and this was the extension past closing; the span an agent could possibly work was 08:00-18:00 either way, so no agent's hours changed.

full_day_schedule._retimed_2026_08_06: Three case batches moved into office hours: 02:00 -> 08:00 (share 0.20), 04:30 -> 09:30 (0.15), 07:00 -> 11:00 (0.15). The remaining three moved only to keep the spread even: 09:30 -> 12:00 (0.15), 12:00 -> 13:30 (0.15), 15:00 unchanged (0.20). Six batches before, six after; shares unedited and still summing to 1.00. Non-batch blocks did not move at all.

Three batches before, three after; shares unedited and still summing to 1.00. model_education_program.description: Stress-tests Claude (data-center) and Gemini (Notebook-X) — the two production AI systems the office exists to evaluate. Runs once per work day at the 'report' block, after that day's question batches.

daily_ai_experience_report.who: every agent who asked at least one question today
daily_ai_experience_report.what: a short, casual fileStatusReport()-style note (1-2 paragraphs) on today's experience asking Claude/Gemini real questions: what worked, what didn't, tone matches the agent's personality.
daily_ai_experience_report.permission_level: private (staff/agents + owner) per CLAUDE.md report tiering — these are internal mood/experience notes, not business-facing.

capability_gap_reporting._meta: SUPERSEDED the old 'model_education_case_study' sub-block 2026-07-18 (Q&A-engine rebuild). No longer batched at end of day from 'the worst N interactions' — each ask-and-evaluate call (agents/agent-base.js askAssignedProject()) decides in real time via workers/gap-reports.js detectCapabilityGap() + the agent's own escalation_threshold (config/agents-config.json, see Step 3 persona differentiation).
capability_gap_reporting.trigger: HARD gaps (no Notebook-X answer at all, or the Claude request itself failed) always flag, any persona. SOFT candidates (a real but weak answer, quality < 0.5) only flag if quality is also below THIS agent's escalation_threshold — sensitive personas (QA, Lead QA) flag more of these than tolerant ones (Standard, Trainee).
capability_gap_reporting.what: a short (2-4 line) HEBREW internal office note, in the flagging agent's own voice via queryGeminiDirect() (Gemini composes the Hebrew — the Groq-routed path is English-only persona flavor): what's missing/wrong, where (topic/notebook), what it teaches. Framed as "the tool I work with isn't good enough here, flagging it for the tool to be fixed" — internal office logic, not a customer-facing incident.
capability_gap_reporting.routing: agent.fileGapReport() persists a `reports` row (type='gap_hebrew', project set). Once per day at this 'report' block, agent-runner.js's fileGapDigests() reads today's rows, groups by project, and commits ONE file per project with entries to reports/gaps/<project>/<date>.md. NEVER a GitHub Issue, for either project — an explicit requirement of this rebuild, unlike the old model_education_case_study which did open one.
capability_gap_reporting.permission_level: special (AI staff + owner) — internal, Hebrew, not business-facing.

spare_time_program.description: Fires whenever an agent has no more assigned cases for the day and no meeting to attend. Two outcomes, chosen per agent:

coworker_interaction.what: one short Gemini call generating a brief in-character exchange between this agent and a related agent (relationships.json partnerships/rivalries preferred), logged as an `interactions` row (type='coworker_chat'). Costs exactly 1 Gemini call.

idle.what: agent goes idle: state is saved as-is, an `interactions` row (type='idle', no query/response) is logged for the daily summary, and ZERO Gemini/Claude calls are made. This is the default and MUST be the only path on Saturdays (force_idle).
idle.token_savings: this is the primary token-discipline lever for spare time, per Launch Decisions.

weekly_summary_program.description: Friday 12:00. Generates the week's executive package and bumps product versions for any asset_pipeline items that reached 'implemented' this week.

outputs.format: markdown, ~10 sections, print-ready (consistent with the existing index.html PDF Export convention — open and use the browser's Print to PDF for an actual 10-page PDF).
outputs.permission_level: private/special — internal weekly package, not for public distribution.

outputs.format: CSV (Excel-openable, no xlsx binary dependency per CLAUDE.md 'no build step, ever'). One row per agent: cases handled, mood start/end, irritation events, happy events, app-call count, comparisons, quality avg.
short markdown, business-facing excerpt (clean framing, no internal mood/score detail).

product_versioning.description: Each admin-tier agent (5-11, can_generate_assets: true) may own at most one 'weekly project' at a time, tracked as an agents/reports/asset-pipeline/board.json entry with a `product_id`. On the Friday weekly_summary_program, any board item whose stage advanced to 'implemented' this week bumps that product's version by +0.01 (starting at 1.00) in year_stats.stats.product_versions, and the board entry's `version` field is updated to match.

guides_program.description: Owner-directed special task for the dormant Architect persona (agent 10) — see CLAUDE.md 'Guides'. Two model calls per guide: a writer persona (chosen by domain, workers/guide-engine.js pickWriterAgentId()) drafts via Gemini; the Architect reviews/finalizes via a DIRECT Anthropic API call (workers/claude-client.js, model claude-sonnet-5, tracked against its OWN $4.50/mo sub-budget — config/token-economy.json guides_claude_budget, workers/model-router.js component:'guides'). Output: markdown files under guides/<domain>/<slug>.md, committed through the existing guarded commitFileToRepo() — same class of write as gap digests.

guide_draft.what: Picks today's topic (capability gaps first, then guides/TOPICS.md fallback — see workers/guide-engine.js selectGuideTopic()), asks the chosen writer persona to draft via Gemini (agent.queryGeminiDirect(), paced through the existing checkGeminiPacingSlot()). Stores the draft in D1 guide_pipeline (status='drafted'); does not commit anything itself.

guide_review.what: Self-healing: if today's draft is missing (missed tick, or Gemini paced out), generates it in the same tick before reviewing (one Gemini + one Claude call in one invocation — well within Cloudflare subrequest limits). The Architect reviews via Claude: APPROVE commits guides/<domain>/<slug>.md and appends any UNVERIFIED sections to guides/_verification-queue.md; REVISE sends fixes back to the writer for ONE revision round then re-reviews; REJECT (or a failed second review) commits the draft + rejection note to guides/_drafts/<slug>.md instead. Never escalates to the owner — fire-and-forget, log and move on.

guide_verify.what: Saturday 08:00 Israel only. Pulls 1-2 items from guides/_verification-queue.md, runs one Claude call per item WITH the web_search server tool for fresh grounding. On success, updates the guide and removes the queue entry; on failure the entry stays for next week.
